title: Ex6 - Open: Marks and channels
text:
Run the code below in a new cell:

```python
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

url = 'https://github.com/muratfirat78/CPP_Datasets/raw/main/auto.xlsx'
dfAuto = pd.read_excel(url)
dfAuto['acceleration'] = dfAuto['acceleration']/10
dfAuto = dfAuto.drop(dfAuto.loc[dfAuto['acceleration'] == 95].index)

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12,8))
ax = fig.add_subplot(111)
ax.scatter(dfAuto['acceleration'], dfAuto['mpg'], color='black')
plt.title('MPG vs. Acceleration')
plt.xlabel('Acceleration')
plt.ylabel('MPG')
plt.show()
```

Look at the scatter plot of the automobile dataset (acceleration vs mpg). Identify: (1) what the marks are, (2) which visual channels are used, and (3) what each channel encodes.
answer: Marks: points/dots. Channels: position x = acceleration, position y = mpg. No color channel in Ex6 — all points are black. Lower acceleration values tend to correspond to lower mpg.
